summary.intent: Land the perf work for the caliper extract/RDT pipeline (streaming `--format rdt`), measure the final combined performance, and resolve the review finding on PR #445 so the held perf work can proceed.
summary.outcome: Streaming rdt shipped as draft PR #447 (gate-large rdt 4.2s to 1.65s, RSS 3.7GB to 1.07GB, byte-identical output). A combined main vs #446+#447 benchmark was taken, but on a noisy machine. #445 conflicts with merged #440 in 8 files, and the worker was sent to resolve that plus the on_demand.rs test-determinism finding.

repo: Commits and pushes need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 because the pre-commit hook otherwise picks rustc 1.98.1 and fails.
`scripts/weekly.py` runs the same rdt path as `extract --format rdt`, so rdt perf gains carry over to the weekly run.
A prop (`Arc<ParsedProp>`) always sits exactly three objects deep in rdt output, so one pretty-printed rendering (indented 6 spaces) can be reused for every occurrence.
serde_json `RawValue` inside the pretty printer emits compact bytes, so it cannot be used to splice stored compact bytes in the canonical writer without changing output (why F15 was skipped).

Byte-identity is checked via `cmp` across 24 combinations (gate-large/chakra-only x rdt/canonical/toon x default/weekly x with/without --no-checker); `durationMs` must be masked in canonical and toon since the base build varies there.
Validation lanes: `just test-rust`, `just test-checker-lane` (includes construct:parity), `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver`.
Merge order matters: #440 (guards) had to land first; #445 (slice 4) conflicts with it, and F5/F6, checker seam, pipeline overlap and Storybook upgrade wait on #445.

code.finding: Removing the hold barrier makes the priority test depend on thread scheduling: the worker may finish warming and start a background request before `Other` is queued, and active requests are not preempted, so the assertion fails spuriously.
Worker request-selection logic; an active request is not preempted, so all test requests must be queued before the worker picks one.
`rdt::write` streams typed structs to a writer, rendering each distinct Arc<ParsedProp> (keyed by address) once in parallel and splicing the bytes as RawValues.

workflow: When benchmarking two builds from separate git worktrees, give each its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR; a shared target dir made the 'combined' build finish in 0.15s because cargo reused main's artifacts.
Interleave A/B runs and report medians with load average; benchmarks taken while workers were building (load 8-18) are only good to about ±0.1s.
Verify gains against noise: #446's 5-7% checker-path gain was within noise on gate-large and Chakra, though --no-checker improved consistently.
Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions; verify state (remote SHA, PR status) before relaying.

friction: The machine was under load (8-18) from concurrent worker builds, so timings were not quiet and the 'well under 2s' target on gate-large (1.81s) could not be confirmed with margin.
Shared cargo target dir between worktrees produced a misleading instant build and had to be redone.
Pre-commit hook picked the wrong rustc (1.98.1) unless MISE_RUST_VERSION was set.
PR #447 showed BLOCKED on Entire Gates; CI and findings were not yet checked.
#445 conflicts with merged #440 in 8 files, blocking the held perf work.
open_items: Resolve #445 conflict (merge main, keep #440 guards) and the on_demand.rs finding: restore a deterministic gate, prove it fails with an injected delay and passes 200 consecutive runs, and audit other semantic tests for the same hazard.
Rerun timings on a quiet machine to confirm the rdt path is well under 2s on gate-large.
Not yet measured: F5 (one-shot tail), F7 (warm snapshot), F9/F11 (pipeline overlap), and the kept-answer rerun (0.25s earlier).
Storybook first answer (~170-190ms) and watch on ButtonProps (~172ms) are over target; F7 expected to fix the first answer, F6 only changes gate harness measurement.
Accuracy with the checker as the default has not been measured; the oracle run is still needed.
Start the held work (F5/F6, checker seam, pipeline overlap, Storybook upgrade) once #445 is settled.
